study_design: Prospective cohort study using the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey Epidemiological Follow-up Study cohort
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Among 3,779 men followed from 1982-84 to 1992, 136 incident cases were identified.
reason: The study prospectively analyzes incident prostate cancer overall. The abstract does not analyze aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, or lethal prostate cancer incidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: In adjusted proportional hazards models, prostate cancer risk was not associated with the vegetable-fruit or red meat-starch pattern, but higher intake of the Southern pattern showed a reduction in risk (3rd versus 1st tertile relative risk, 0.6; 95% confidence interval, 0.4-1.1; trend P = 0.08) that approached statistical significance.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied Western-pattern row appears to correspond to the red meat-starch pattern, and the analyzed endpoint is overall incident prostate cancer. The abstract does not provide a numeric estimate for that pattern.
